subject.title: [Feature]: Support running OpenClaw on devices without Linux / Node.js (inspired by MimiClaw)

question: Should OpenClaw commit to an externally implementable, versioned agent-runtime contract for non-Node and bare-metal ports, or keep the supported product boundary as a Node-hosted TypeScript orchestration system?
rationale: The request is a large cross-cutting product and compatibility boundary, not a missing local extension hook; current source provides reusable internal code but no agreed public ABI or supported portable capability set.

options.title: Sponsor a staged external-runtime design
options.body: Define the portable minimum contract, capability negotiation, security model, and conformance proof before accepting implementation work.

options.title: Keep Node as the supported runtime
options.body: Retain the current architecture and direct cross-language extension needs to the narrower plugin-process boundary where appropriate.

options.title: Limit scope to plugin RPC first
options.body: Advance https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/98004 as a Node-hosted plugin boundary, while explicitly deferring bare-metal runtime compatibility.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a staged external-runtime design
recommendation.body: Define the portable minimum contract, capability negotiation, security model, and conformance proof before accepting implementation work.

likelyOwner.reason: Existing issue guidance and the merged agent-runtime extraction connect steipete most directly to the required architecture decision.
